plain_summary: This page details the calculation methodology for berth dues, specifying the source documents required from Terminal Operators for different vessel types (bulk/break bulk, container, other). It outlines how to calculate the chargeable period for berth dues by deducting cargo working hours (including free periods) from the total time a vessel is in port. The page also lists several exemptions from berth dues, such as for SAPS/SANDF vessels, vessels taking stores/fuel (for 48 hours), and medical/research vessels. Additionally, it introduces specific berth dues for vessels shipping ore at the Saldanha ore loading jetty, charged per hour based on summer dead-mass tonnage under certain conditions (e.g., delays exceeding two hours). Finally, it mandates the submission of a Statement of Facts within 24 hours of departure and specifies a fee for non-submission.

formulas.formula_as_written: Chargeable Period (hours) = Period vessel is in port (hours) - (Number of hours worked as per source document (hours) + Free periods before cargo working (hours) + Free periods after cargo working (hours))
formulas.what_it_calculates: The chargeable period for berth dues, which is then multiplied by the rates defined on page 22.
parameters_used: Number of hours worked as per source document (hours)
formulas.rounding_or_conditions: The resulting chargeable period is then applied to the rates per 100 tons (from page 22) for each 24-hour period or part thereof. Free periods are 6 cargo working hours before and 6 after for non-container berths, 2 cargo working hours for container berths (from page 22).
